Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: What is the mug’s position relative to the headphones in the edited image?
node.criteria: complete if the mug is to the right of the headphones; partial if it has moved toward the right but is not to their right; absent if there is no progress toward moving it right; unknown if the image does not provide sufficient evidence. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is incomplete (`(...)`) and the node’s criterion only checks the mug’s final position. In the edited image, the mug on the right is to the right of the headphones, but the original blue mug remains as a blurred/ghosted object on the left and another mug appears near the headphones. Thus the traces’ confident “complete” judgment may be overlooking whether the requested mug was actually moved, rather than duplicated or left behind; the reference `partial` is an aggregate constraint, not proof of a specific atomic interpretation. Repair the binding to identify the mug from the source (the blue mug left of the headphones), and make the decision criterion compare source and edited images for that same object, distinguishing genuine movement toward/right of the headphones from persistence, duplication, or an ambiguous identity. Preserve an unknown/unresolved outcome when identity or movement cannot be established; do not infer partial progress merely from low confidence or variation. The five identical, high-confidence traces indicate a systematic criterion/evidence blind spot, not a transport or dependency failure."}
